evidence: The smallest compliant submission is substantial: instruction.md:1-5 requires source editing, execution and saved versions; environment/instructions/ui.md:3-15 requires an authored document surface, selection, multi-caret editing, undo, find/replace, semantic colouring and semantics-preserving formatting; behaviour.md:3-9 requires isolated JS/HTML execution, error reporting, last-good recovery, durable shared saves, conflicts and revision restores. integration.md:7-9 requires independent-context sharing and SQLite persistence. A static page or one CRUD screen cannot satisfy those public requirements. The zero-weight render gate in tests/gates/render/judge.toml:17-24 requires browser-authored JavaScript with a computed interactive preview and console output; the constraints gate at :17-33 requires a custom editor plus a freshly read shared saved record. tests/scoring.toml:1-10 and tests/tools/score.py:41-48 give zero reward if either gate or the functional floor fails. Adversarial case: a custom but rudimentary editor and JS runner with an in-memory server library might clear the gates and earn limited partial credit while failing restart/history; that still entails a working editor, execution and cross-context server behavior, not a static mock or trivial tweak. A compliant alternative using a custom DOM/canvas editor, isolated preview and SQLite is allowed by the brief's choice of routes, layout and tools (policy.md:3-5). The cited frozen files and workbook/skill hashes match manifest.json. No raw-evidence-index.json or full configured judge/weak-app run was present, so the anti-stub reward behavior has not been empirically measured; this is the remaining risk, not a demonstrated row-7 defect.
